title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ན (Derge Tengyur, vol. 13)

It belongs on a tantra-commentary shelf. catalog_metadata.collections is empty, and the record is a whole volume with no work titles or authors.
structure_note: 605 records, 604 with OCR and 604 translated, so one page (probably the cover or label) has no text. Every page read has the right leaf. tr_errors.english: the Vajra Moon of Stainless Light <note>original: "Vajracandra Vimalaprabha"</note>
tr_errors.problem: the note labels a Sanskrit back-reconstruction as 'original', but the page is Tibetan

tr_errors.problem: the verse line is forced: it says the winds arise as the twelve links, and 'of the family' is a misparse

tr_errors.english: the six buddha families
tr_errors.problem: 'buddha' is added

tr_errors.english: In order to purify the Vajracharya
tr_errors.problem: too literal: the sense is to qualify or make the student a vajra master, not to purify an existing one

tr_errors.english: The first is freedom from passion; then great passion
tr_errors.problem: these are epithets (as in the Nāmasaṃgīti) made into a sequence

book_verdict: All four leaves are right and carry a clean reference e-text. The English is a careful, mostly literal rendering of a Kālacakra-cycle commentary, with only small slips.
reader_summary: This is one volume of the Derge Tengyur's tantra commentaries; the sampled leaves read like the Vimalaprabhā tradition (the sixteen kāyas, the four joys, initiation, the six-branch yoga). The Tibetan is the Esukhia e-text and matches each scan line for line. The English follows it closely enough to trust for sense, though the Sanskrit glosses in the notes are the model's own additions.

title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཙ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 18)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur rgyud 'grel volume tsa: Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka-cycle commentaries (the third initiation, consort characteristics and siddhis, a list of purifying mantras, Garuḍa-faced Heruka rites, phur pa). It belongs on the shelf. collections is empty.
structure_note: 463 records, 462 with OCR and translated. The leaves are right, and the margin number runs one ahead of page_number (68 shows 69, 158 shows 159, 396 shows 397). There is no splice. p.396 holds the colophon of chapter 34 ('ལེའུ་སུམ་ཅུ་རྩ་བཞིའི་འགྲེལ་པའོ') and the start of the next section, as the image shows.

tr_errors.english: joining the tips of the central channel <note>the union of the central channels of the practitioners</note>
tr_errors.problem: the note interprets beyond what the text says

tr_errors.english: the supreme secret wisdom is realized
tr_errors.problem: 'is realized' is added; the source runs on into the next clause

tr_errors.english: the secret path of the <term>Rigden</term> <gloss>Kalki or Lineage Holder</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: rigs ldan here means a person of the (tantric) family, a qualified practitioner. The gloss brings in the Kalki kings of Shambhala, who are not on this Heruka-cycle page.

tr_errors.english: the "brother" <note>likely referring to a spiritual peer or a specific male energy</note>
tr_errors.problem: a hedged note on a term the model could not place

tr_errors.english: Regarding Siddhi, she manifests the supreme attainment
tr_errors.problem: makes the consort the subject of the siddhi clause

other.note: Opening <meta> is a free summary ('secret paths of the Vidyadhara'), not a continuity note, and '...becomes <note>referring to a spiritual transformation or realization</note>' glosses a seam fragment
The list of common siddhis is set as a bulleted list; the source is prose

ocr_errors.image: unclear at this resolution; the series (mind, then speech, then body) requires ངག (speech) here
ocr_errors.problem: speech is probably dropped or misread in the 13th-mantra line, though it may be the block's own reading

tr_errors.english: the thirteenth mantra is purification; it is said, "All phenomena are purified by the pure."
tr_errors.problem: renders a defective line fluently instead of flagging it; the parallel series implies 'purified by speech'

tr_errors.english: in the Southeast is Yamadanti ... In the Northwest is Yamadhadi
tr_errors.problem: the Sanskrit names are swapped: brtan ma is Yamadāḍhī, mche ba is Yamadaṃṣṭrī

book_verdict: The right leaves carry a reference-quality transcription. The translation is faithful in substance, but its glosses sometimes import the wrong context: Kalki on a Heruka page, and swapped goddess names.
reader_summary: This is a Derge Tengyur volume of Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka-cycle commentaries: initiation procedure, consort lore, purifying mantras, and phur pa and weather rites. The Tibetan is the right text for every scan. The English is usable for sense, but the glosses in its notes and the Sanskrit names it adds are not reliable: one gloss brings in the Shambhala Kalkis and two goddess names are swapped.

book_verdict: The leaves are right and the transcriptions clean. But the e-text's {variant,variant} markup shows in the OCR pane, and the Hevajra yoginī song has speaker and addressee confused.
reader_summary: This is a Derge Tengyur volume of Hevajra-cycle ritual and commentary: iconography for painted maṇḍalas, the generation stage, the yoginīs' song, consecration. The Tibetan is the right text, but the transcription shows the e-text's editorial brackets ({ཡི་དགས་,ཡི་དྭགས་}) inline. The English is sound for the ritual prose but misreads who speaks in the liturgical verses, so the verse passages need checking.

title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ལི (Derge Tengyur, vol. 57)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur rgyud 'grel volume li: Yoga-tantra maṇḍala ritual of the Vajradhātu/Vairocana type (the Tathāgata epithets, empowerments, laying the maṇḍala lines, thrones of the five Buddhas, homa). It belongs on the shelf. collections is empty.
structure_note: 703 records, 702 with OCR and translated. The leaves are right, and the margin number runs one ahead of page_number (84 shows 85, 221 shows 222, 504 shows 505, 610 shows 611). Nothing else stands out.

tr_errors.english: To the Mother <note>This refers to the primary female deity or the essence of wisdom</note>
tr_errors.problem: the page opens mid-word (most likely [སྐད་ཅིག་]མ་གཅིག་ལ, 'in a single instant'). The translator invents 'the Mother' and adds an explanatory note.

tr_errors.problem: a seam fragment explained by a speculative note

other.note: <meta> asserts the text is 'likely part of the Guhyasamaja'. The page is a Vajradhātu-type Yoga-tantra maṇḍala, with lion, elephant, horse and peacock thrones for the five Buddhas around Vairocana. This is invented, wrong attribution.

tr_errors.english: With the body held straight, <unclear>various</unclear>
tr_errors.problem: the translator marks a clear seam word as <unclear>

book_verdict: The leaves are right and the transcription clean. The ritual instructions are translated accurately, with the directions and sequence of the line-laying intact. The weak spots are page-top fragments that the translator explains with invented notes, and a wrong attribution to Guhyasamāja in one meta note.
reader_summary: This is a Derge Tengyur volume of Yoga-tantra maṇḍala ritual in the Vajradhātu/Vairocana line: empowerment, laying the maṇḍala's lines, the thrones of the five Buddhas, fire offerings. The Tibetan is the right text for every scan. The English is reliable for procedure, but notes at page breaks sometimes invent a meaning for a half-word, and one note names the wrong tantra cycle.
